A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain the main text and Appendices A–M. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison, including recovery of v1's clipped Appendix I examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original steering experiments across 23 language models, rhyming and question-answering results, attention interventions, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main comparisons and the appendix experiments on attention, tokenization, alternative steering, and subject-verb agreement.

M1.justification: The described mean-activation-difference steering procedure, single-token intervention, and layer selection are retained. The corrected summation subscript in Section 3.3 repairs the mathematical statement of the procedure already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same rhyme families, suggestive and neutral noun questions, specific-word rhyming scenarios, and arithmetic subject-verb agreement task in Appendix L.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same unsteered controls and alternative probe-weight and SAE steering examples in Appendix I. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Model configurations, splits, metrics, and intervention settings are unchanged. Both retain the 85/20 rhyming split, 50 generations per test prompt, and the same question-answering and appendix protocols.

E4.justification: The training-size sensitivity, attention ablation, metric correlations, tokenization controls, specific-word steering, SAE analyses, and subject-verb control experiment are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Existing statistical reporting and plotted uncertainty displays are unchanged. v2 introduces no additional run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the plotted results retain their values and findings, including Table 1's 59–93% patching recovery and Appendix I's 832/1000 SAE-steering successes. Appendix I's newly readable examples contain the same underlying output text.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the first summation's category from C1 to C2. This removes an identically zero C1-minus-C1 expression and expresses target-minus-source activations. The planning definitions and remaining mathematical content are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: scalable planning metrics, evidence across 23 models down to 1B parameters, and manipulation of forward and backward planning.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications remain unchanged, including weak specific-word steering in Appendix H, distributed answer planning in Appendix K, and unresolved generality of the identified planning circuits in Section 4.6.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement explicitly identifies OpenReview supplementary material and adds a GitHub URL for code, data, and outputs. This revises access instructions beyond v1's directory pointers; it does not establish changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes to Hanna and Ameisen, Kambhampati et al., and the phonetic-representation reference update bibliographic metadata and citation labels for the same works.

P1.justification: v2 revises the acknowledgements and reproducibility wording and makes limited punctuation and bibliographic corrections. The scientific narrative, terminology, and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block is rearranged, several main-text figures move relative to surrounding prose, and Appendix I outputs are wrapped to reveal previously clipped text. The figures, tables, and captions retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the duplicated category subscript in Section 3.3, supplies clearer code/data access instructions, and makes clipped Appendix I examples readable. These provide limited improvements in mathematical accuracy and usability while leaving the empirical evidence and conclusions unchanged.
